short: The value GST is charged on, after discounts and before tax.
seoTitle: Taxable Value — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Taxable value is the amount on which GST is calculated for a supply. An error here quietly propagates through all of them.
definition: Taxable value is the amount on which GST is calculated for a supply. It is the price charged after any discount given at or before the time of supply, and before the tax itself is added.
bodyHtml:
Why Taxable Value matters

Every downstream number depends on this base — the tax charged, the invoice total, the value reported in returns and the credit your customer claims. An error here quietly propagates through all of them.

Taxable Value formula

Taxable value = Gross price − Discount at the time of supply

Add incidental charges recovered from the customer before applying the tax rate.

How Taxable Value works in practice

Discounts agreed at the time of billing reduce taxable value; discounts given afterwards need a credit note to have the same effect. Freight, packing and similar charges recovered from the customer generally form part of the value.

faq.question: Are delivery charges part of taxable value?
faq.answer: Charges you recover from the customer as part of the supply generally are, and are taxed at the same rate as the main supply.

faq.question: How do post-sale discounts affect taxable value?
faq.answer: They reduce it only through a credit note, subject to the conditions for such discounts.
